title: DBT model merging data in snowflake table that use auto increment column
body:

title: dbt snapshot creates duplicate dbt_scd_id even though source query returns no duplicates
body:
I'm creating a dbt snapshot from a Snowflake source table. The source table receives a full export regularly, and it contains two important columns: id and inserted_at_utc. Each export inserts a new full dataset.

To snapshot only the latest export, I use this macro:

{% macro snapshot_latest_record(
    source_name,
    table_name,
    timestamp_column='inserted_at_utc',
    exclude_columns='inserted_at_utc'
) %}

    SELECT
        * EXCLUDE ({{ exclude_columns }})
    FROM {{ source(source_name, table_name) }}
    WHERE {{ timestamp_column }} = (
        SELECT MAX({{ timestamp_column }})
        FROM {{ source(source_name, table_name) }}
    )

{% endmacro %}

My snapshot model:

{% snapshot snap_boond__agencies %}

  {{
    config(
      target_schema='SNAPSHOT',
      strategy='check',
      unique_key='ID',
      check_cols='all',
      invalidate_hard_deletes=True,
    )
  }}

  {{ snapshot_latest_record('<source_name>', '<table_name>') }}

{% endsnapshot %}

To verify that the latest export contains no duplicates, I run:

SELECT 
    ID,
    COUNT(*) AS cnt
FROM (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        * EXCLUDE (inserted_at_utc)
    FROM <my_table>
    WHERE inserted_at_utc = (
        SELECT MAX(inserted_at_utc)
        FROM <my_table>
    )
    QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
        PARTITION BY ID
        ORDER BY inserted_at_utc DESC, ID DESC
    ) = 1
)
GROUP BY ID
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

This query returns no results, so the source data is not duplicated.

However, dbt still fails with duplicate dbt_scd_id errors:

Failure in test unique_snap_boond__agencies_DBT_SCD_ID
Got 5 results, configured to fail if != 0

And even a full refresh fails:

Database Error in snapshot snap_boond__agencies
100090 (42P18): Duplicate row detected during DML action
Row Values: [redacted]

If the macro returns only one row per ID, why is dbt generating duplicate dbt_scd_id values during the snapshot? What could cause duplicates inside the snapshot table even when the source query itself contains none ?

title: How can I set up an ETL process for DataFrames (dbt or alternative tools)?
body:
Question: I'm currently working on a dashboard prototype and storing data from a 22-page PDF document as 22 separate DataFrames. These DataFrames should undergo an ETL process (especially data type conversions) on every import before being written to the database.

My initial approach was to use dbt seeds and/or models. However, dbt loads the seed CSV directly into the SQLite database without my prior transformations taking effect. I want to transform first and then load.

Setup:

* Data source: 22 DataFrames extracted from PDF tables

* Database: SQLite (for prototype only)

* ETL/ELT tool: preferably dbt, but not mandatory

* Language: Python Problem: How can I set up an ETL workflow where DataFrames are processed and transformed directly without having to load them into dbt as CSV (seeds) beforehand?

Is there a way to integrate DataFrames directly into a dbt model process? If not, what alternative tools are suitable (e.g., Airflow, Dagster, Prefect, pandas-based ETL pipelines, etc.)?

Previous attempts:

* dbt seed: loads CSV directly into the database → transformations don't work

* dbt models: only work if the data is already in the database, which I want to avoid

* Currently: manual type conversions in Python (float, int, string, datetime)

Looking for: Best practices or tool recommendations for directly transforming DataFrames and then loading them into SQLite – with or without dbt.
